key_insight: Transformer-based quantum circuit synthesis works well when approximate outputs can be repaired, but exact discrete correctness breaks down as autoregressive decoding error accumulates with circuit length.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum compilation, this means sequence models are useful only if paired with verification, search, or post-processing; otherwise exact-equivalence guarantees become unreliable on longer circuits.
method: 44.8M-parameter encoder-decoder transformer with structured circuit tokenization
Evaluated on parameterized circuits (2–6 qubits) and Clifford+T circuits (3–6 qubits)
Compared hybrid post-processing, candidate generation plus equivalence checking, and larger training sets
evidence_signal: On parameterized circuits, the hybrid method reached median fidelity 1.000 for 3–6 qubit cases; on Clifford+T circuits, exact match fell from 88% at ≤9 gates to near zero beyond 26 gates, with multi-candidate verification improving exact match from 7% to 22.5% and 2.5× more data raising it to 39.5%.
watch_item: Even with more data or inference-time search, exact equivalence still degrades sharply for longer targets, so deployment should include formal verification or alternative decoding strategies rather than relying on single-pass generation.
paper_title: When Close Enough Is Not Enough: Autoregressive Drift in Quantum Circuit Synthesis
